items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Invited for this month's cover picture is the group of Federico Calle‐Vallejo and Francesc Illas from the University of Barcelona (Spain). The cover picture shows that there are three ways of simulating the energy landscape of oxygen reduction to hydrogen peroxide with density functional theory: without any corrections (yellow), with O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> corrections (yellow/red), and with O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> and H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> corrections (red); only the latter agrees with experiments. Read the full text of the Research Article at <jats:ext-link xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink" xlink:href="https://doi.org/10.1002/celc.202200210">10.1002/celc.202200210</jats:ext-link></jats:p>
title: Gas‐phase errors affect DFT‐based electrocatalysis models of oxygen reduction to hydrogen peroxide

items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Electrochemical production of H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> is more benign and affordable than the conventional route, yet its adoption requires the discovery of robust, cost‐effective catalysts. DFT‐based models lead to conspicuous breakthroughs but had some known limitations, for instance the poor description of molecules with certain chemical bonds. Here, the errors in H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> and O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> displayed by various GGAs, meta‐GGAs and hybrids were assessed and semi empirically corrected. The errors in O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> with respect to experiments were in the range of −0.95 to −0.22 eV, whereas those in H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> spanned from −0.53 to −0.04 eV. Thus, single and double O−O bonds were poorly described in general, and the errors were nearly twice as negative for double bonds. Furthermore, these errors introduced large deviations in the predictions of free energies for O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> reduction to H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>, and the equilibrium potentials and optimal adsorption energies of *OOH could either be sizably overestimated or underestimated.</jats:p>
title: Gas‐Phase Errors Affect DFT‐Based Electrocatalysis Models of Oxygen Reduction to Hydrogen Peroxide
